cards.front: Recall a key point about Palaeozoic & Mesozoic Eras
cards.back: The Palaeozoic Era (541-252 Ma): Cambrian explosion of hard-bodied life, Silurian marine life, Devonian age of fish and early land plants, Carboniferous coal forests, Permian mass extinction

cards.front: Recall a key point about Palaeozoic & Mesozoic Eras
cards.back: The Cambrian explosion (~541 Ma): rapid diversification of life with hard shells and skeletons, making fossilisation much more common

cards.front: Recall a key point about Palaeozoic & Mesozoic Eras
cards.back: The Carboniferous (359-299 Ma): warm, humid climate; vast swamp forests of ferns, horsetails and clubmosses formed today's coal deposits

cards.front: Recall a key point about Palaeozoic & Mesozoic Eras
cards.back: The Permian-Triassic mass extinction (~252 Ma): the 'Great Dying' eliminated ~96% of marine species, caused by massive volcanism (Siberian Traps) and climate change

cards.front: Recall a key point about Palaeozoic & Mesozoic Eras
cards.back: The Mesozoic Era (252-66 Ma): Triassic (recovery and early dinosaurs), Jurassic (age of dinosaurs and ammonites), Cretaceous (flowering plants, T-rex)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Palaeozoic & Mesozoic Eras
cards.back: Ammonites are key Mesozoic index fossils: they evolved rapidly and were globally distributed, allowing precise correlation of Jurassic and Cretaceous rocks

cards.front: What should you know about gcse geology exam tips — palaeozoic & mesozoic eras?
cards.back: 1. For Palaeozoic & Mesozoic Eras questions, use correct geological terminology and classify features precisely 2. Reference specific geological time periods and processes 3. When interpreting data, consider the quality and limitations of the evidence 4. Apply your understanding of Palaeozoic & Mesozoic Eras to fieldwork observations and map data 5. For evaluation, weigh competing geological theories with evidence
Describe the key events of the Palaeozoic and Mesozoic eras and explain the significance of the Permian mass extinction. [6 marks]
